title: Alphonso Davies available for Canada’s second World Cup game against Qatar – Jesse Marsch
content:
VANCOUVER — Canada captain Alphonso Davies will be available for his country’s second World Cup game against Qatar on Thursday.

“(Davies) has been in training this week,” Canada head coach Jesse Marsch said during a press conference. “We’ll see how the match goes and then make a decision on how we would choose to use them (Davies and centre-back Moïse Bombito).”

Davies was injured during the second leg of Bayern Munich’s Champions League semi-final against Paris Saint-Germain on May 6. The left-back’s timeline for recovery was expected to be 4-6 weeks. Wednesday’s press conference marked exactly six weeks since Davies sustained his injury.

Davies’ availability has been a fertile topic of discourse after arriving in Canada camp on June 1. Marsch said when the team’s World Cup roster was announced that Davies would play at some point and yet the 25-year-old has remained in return-to-play protocol. That means he has trained both with the team and on his own with Matthias Blankenburg, an independent specialist trainer, as part of an arrangement between Bayern, Davies and Canada Soccer.

While Bombito also did not play in Canada’s opener against Bosnia and Herzegovina, a 1-1 draw, he did remain in full training for Canada in the lead-up to Thursday’s game against Qatar. Marsch confirmed on Wednesday that Bombito would be available to play against Qatar.

When Davies has trained in Vancouver, he has looked far more nimble and powerful than he did during Canada’s camp in Montreal. Davies last played for Canada in March 2025 during the Nations League third-place game against the United States, in which he tore his ACL.

Ahead of Tuesday’s training session, Canada Soccer said it would no longer be providing updates on Davies’ injury status. The organization had previously given daily updates before training on Davies and the rest of Canada’s players.

“Alphonso is looking really good, right? And so it’s just a matter of ‘OK, what kind of game is it, what kind of moment is it, and how do we feel Alphonso can contribute right now?’ But he’s ready, he’ll be available,” Marsch said.

Canada Soccer’s approach to Davies’ health updates suggests an element of gamesmanship during the World Cup. Marsch continued to keep possible lineup changes close to his vest on Wednesday, stating “I’m not giving that information” when asked if he would make changes from his starting XI in Canada’s World Cup opener against Bosnia and Herzegovina on Friday.

Canada Soccer did, however, provide an update on centre-back Alfie Jones on Tuesday, stating he was in a “personal recovery day.”

Jones did not train with Canada on Wednesday and Marsch said that the Middlesbrough defender will not play against Qatar. The centre-back has made just one appearance — as a substitute in Canada’s June 1 friendly against Uzbekistan — since an ankle injury and ensuing surgery. Jones has since suffered a setback in his recovery.
